clue.text: Sequence of possible events with cranes moving satellite

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift position, so this word's order is rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
Io is one of the moons of Jupiter

explanation.surface: Construction cranes swing a satellite into place, a set of events someone might plan for.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged lifting machines come first and the Jovian moon IO finishes the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A planned or imagined chain of happenings is exactly what a forecaster or planner calls this kind of outline.

clue.text: Land in the water when one's left suspended in the middle

indicators.note: only the central character of the word is wanted, the one at its exact centre

blocks.note: I is one, plus the 's
L is the standard abbreviation for left
the fifth of nine letters sits at the centre

explanation.surface: Someone lands in the sea and is left hanging, dangling halfway down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' gives I'S, apostrophe dropped; 'left' is L; the centre letter of 'suspended' is E.
explanation.definitionFit: An island is a piece of ground surrounded by sea or lake, and this short poetic word names it.

clue.text: Throw out unknown dignitary

indicators.note: something put out of shape is disordered, so these letters get rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
algebra uses x, y and z as unknowns

explanation.surface: An order to eject some unnamed VIP from a function.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw out' looks like one phrasal verb; 'out' is really the signal to shuffle THROW plus the algebraic unknown Y.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a worthy is an important or distinguished local figure, often used slightly mockingly.

clue.text: Rashly, leader has point inserted in official record

indicators.note: something inserted is put inside something else, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a head is the person in charge
a ship's or official log is a formal record
N, north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A rash leader makes a point that ends up in the official minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rashly' opens the clue as if describing how the leader acts, but it is the definition; N is the usual crossword compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: To act this way is to rush in without thinking, hurtling forward impetuously and recklessly.

clue.text: Leaving to collect small women's group, not even mums, to take a dip

indicators.note: to collect things is to gather them in, so the outer word holds the rest
dropping the even-numbered positions keeps only the odd ones

blocks.note: going means departing
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothes labels
the WI is the Women's Institute, a British community organisation
first and third letters

explanation.surface: A mothers' group outing where the mums stay behind and someone heads off for a swim.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer word splits after its first two letters to take in the others. The Women's Institute is a British organisation known for jam-making and village halls.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a dip is the casual idiom for a short bathe, the same activity as heading off for a swim.

clue.text: Opening ground, authorise ore to be extracted

indicators.note: something ground is crushed into pieces, so the letters come out reshaped
extracting removes material, so some letters are taken away

blocks.note: taken as written
these three letters are removed

explanation.surface: Breaking ground at a mine, with permission given to dig out the ore.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove O, R, E from AUTHORISE to leave AUTHIS, then rearrange. 'Ground' looks like soil in a mining picture, but it is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiatus is a gap or break, so it can mean an aperture or opening as well as a pause.

clue.text: Cutters with ship going round Ross Island cape capsized

indicators.note: a capsized boat is upside down, so in a down-turned or flipped sense the letters run backwards
to go round something is to encircle it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the abbreviation for island
C is the abbreviation for cape on maps
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: An Antarctic voyage near Ross Island, where an icebreaker meets disaster off a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ross Island' looks like the real Antarctic place, but the two words are used separately, the second shrinking to its abbreviation before everything is flipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Scissors are a common household tool for cutting paper or cloth, so they are cutters.

clue.text: Vicar's upset collecting one pound in coins

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, and in a down clue overturning flips the letters end to end
to collect is to take in, so the outer part gathers something inside it

blocks.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a vicar's title, plus the 's
Roman numeral one
L, from Latin libra, is the pound sign

explanation.surface: A clergyman gets upset at finding just a pound in the collection plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads as the vicar's mood, but it flips REVS to SVER, which then takes in I and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Silver is the general British term for small change, the coins of lower value as a group.

clue.text: Toxic shock after ecstasy is unusual

indicators.note: a shock jolts things out of place, leaving the letters jumbled

blocks.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning about toxic shock syndrome after taking ecstasy, which is not a common outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toxic shock' looks like the medical condition; it is TOXIC with its letters jolted, placed after E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exotic is strikingly unfamiliar or foreign, so it is out of the ordinary.

clue.text: United holding lead in Championship previously

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it within, so one part surrounds the other
the lead is what goes first, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: united things are made one
its first letter

explanation.surface: A football team, United, who were once top of the Championship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like a club name; here it means made into ONE. The Championship is English football's second tier.
explanation.definitionFit: Once as an adverb means at some time in the past, formerly, the same sense as earlier.

clue.text: Patronise lecture by Spooner's municipal party?

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so initial sounds trade places

blocks.note: a lecture is a talk
a town do is a civic party; swap its first sounds

explanation.surface: A condescending speech given at the town council's party.
explanation.walkthrough: TOWN DO, with T and D exchanged, becomes DOWN TO. 'Do' is British slang for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak to someone condescendingly as if they were less intelligent is the idiom for being patronising.

clue.text: Heading off unwell during test is crafty

indicators.note: with its heading off a word loses its first letter
during means in the course of, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: unwell means sick; drop the first letter
to try is to test

explanation.surface: A student leaves the exam hall feeling ill, a sly ruse to dodge the test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' looks like someone leaving the room; it means the first letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricky person is cunning and deceitful, full of tricks, the same as being crafty.

clue.text: Try to get to sleep in nobleman's pile, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, so the spelling follows how the words are spoken

blocks.note: a count is a nobleman and a heap is a pile

explanation.surface: An insomniac guest tossing and turning in some aristocrat's stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pile' looks like a grand country house; here it means a heap. Said aloud, COUNT'S HEAP runs together as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Imagining sheep jumping a fence and numbering them is the traditional remedy for insomnia.

clue.text: Pudding seems not to be cooked

indicators.note: cooked means doctored or falsified, so the letters are tampered with

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dessert that appears to be raw, served without being baked.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton mess is a British dessert of crushed meringue, strawberries and cream, named after Eton College. Fittingly, it needs no cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain pudding is the general word for dessert, and this strawberry-meringue dish is a classic summer example.

clue.text: Little girl's dog carrying lead, oddly comical

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside another
oddly points to the odd-numbered positions, first and third

blocks.note: Jo is a short girl's name
a cur is a mongrel dog
first and third letters

explanation.surface: A little girl's puppy trotting along with its lead in its mouth, looking funny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like the dog's leash and also hints at a first letter; here only its odd letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Jocular describes a joking, humorous manner, so it is a close synonym of funny or amusing.

clue.text: New matador runs around, haphazardly

indicators.note: running around is darting all over the place, so the letters scatter into a fresh order

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
taken as written

explanation.surface: A novice bullfighter dashing wildly round the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' might be read as R for runs; it is part of the shuffle signal, and the extra letter comes from N.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without plan, order or method is the sense of the idiom, matching chaotic carelessness.

clue.text: Opposed to profit in a way

indicators.note: something in another thing lies inside it, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: taken as written
a gain is a profit
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone objecting to profiteering, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a way' reads as a hedge meaning 'somewhat'; really the profit sits inside the two other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: As a preposition, against expresses opposition or hostility, so it substitutes for opposed to in a sentence.

clue.text: Military unit is one of four in southern front that's shelled

indicators.note: being in something means being enclosed by it, so one part goes inside
shelling a nut strips its outer casing, leaving only the inner letters

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
a quad is a quadruplet, one of four babies born together
the word without its outer letters

explanation.surface: A wartime army unit pinned down by artillery on the southern front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shelled' suggests bombardment in the military picture; it means peeled, so the word loses its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A squadron is a body of troops, ships or aircraft, a standard division within the armed forces.

clue.text: Unlocked desperate need to pursue work

indicators.note: a desperate person is frantic and wild, so these letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone desperate for work finally finds a door open to them.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'to pursue' means to come after, so the jumbled letters follow OP.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlocking a door or box is releasing its fastening, and in the past tense that is simply having opened it.

clue.text: Hit on perfect comeback to sweet-talk

indicators.note: a comeback is a return journey, so the letters travel back the way they came

blocks.note: to butt is to hit with the head
pure means flawless

explanation.surface: Someone lands on the perfect witty reply to charm another person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit on' looks like a phrasal verb meaning discover or flirt; here 'hit' is BUTT and 'on' just places the next piece after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both expressions mean flattering someone, usually in order to win a favour from them.

clue.text: Chauffeur in a limousine's shown place to go

indicators.note: what is shown is on display, so the letters are visible within the text

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the next three

explanation.surface: A chauffeur in a limo is directed to the right destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place to go' looks like a destination for the driver; it is the polite euphemism for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To go is a common euphemism for relieving oneself, and this fixture in a gents' toilet is where men do so.

clue.text: Tackle occasional roguery with severity

indicators.note: occasional means now and then, so only every other letter is kept

blocks.note: rig is equipment, gear or tackle
second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Clamping down hard on the odd bit of misbehaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tackle' reads as a verb meaning deal with; here it is a noun, fishing or sailing gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigour means strictness or harshness in applying rules, the same quality as severity in treatment.

clue.text: Frightful rotter makes angry reply

indicators.note: something frightful is a dreadful mess, so the letters are put in disarray

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An awful cad snaps back with a furious answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frightful rotter' sounds like old-fashioned British slang for a cad; the adjective is the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A retort is a sharp or cutting reply, often made in anger or in kind.

clue.text: Fine nights at sea with angling gear

indicators.note: to be at sea is to be confused, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Pleasant evenings spent out on a boat with rod and tackle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' fits the fishing scene literally but is the shuffle signal for FINE NIGHTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Angling means fishing with hook and line, and a mesh used to land the catch is part of that kit.

clue.text: Lift's free with key

blocks.note: to rid is to free from
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: An elevator that can be used at no cost with a pass key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' looks like a British elevator; here it means a free car journey, as in 'give someone a lift'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being offered a lift means being driven somewhere by someone, which is the same as being given a trip in their car.

clue.text: Exceptional acceleration in luxury car with electric starter

indicators.note: being in something means lying inside its boundaries, so one piece is enclosed
a starter comes at the beginning, so only the first letter is taken

blocks.note: a is the symbol for acceleration in physics
RR is Rolls-Royce, the luxury British car maker
its first letter

explanation.surface: A luxury electric car with remarkable pick-up off the line.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside RR and E follows. 'Starter' looks like a car's starter motor in the motoring picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rare is uncommon or seldom found, so it stands out as unusually good or out of the ordinary.

clue.text: A last letter has girl and English boy describing love in summerhouse

blocks.note: G is a dictionary abbreviation for girl
taken as written
Z ends the alphabet
E is the abbreviation for English
B is a dictionary abbreviation for boy
love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A boy and girl exchange a love letter in a garden pavilion.
explanation.walkthrough: Single-letter pieces: G and B are dictionary abbreviations for girl and boy, and Z is the alphabet's last letter. The pieces are rearranged in reading order here to G, A, Z, E, B, O.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazebo is a small open garden building or pavilion, a kind of summerhouse for sitting outdoors.

clue.text: Development happens here when ship enters dead space

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: d is the abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies
Noah's ark was a ship
room means space

explanation.surface: A vessel drifting into a lifeless region of space while something evolves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Development' suggests growth or building; it is the photographic process of bringing out images from film.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographers process film in a light-proof chamber, so the place where film is processed is this room.
